strings: Galgar's Cactus Apple Surprise is a straightforward errand undertaken by young warriors and novices in the sun-baked Valley of Trials. Seeking relief from Durotar's punishing heat, the orc Galgar enlists travelers to gather wild cactus apples so he can prepare his famed refreshing treat. The task teaches fresh recruits how to forage and survive in an arid land.

The crimson dirt of the Valley of Trials is notoriously merciless. Between rigorous combat drills and fierce trials against native beasts, exhaustion and dehydration set in quickly. For young orcs and Darkspear trolls taking their first steps as defenders of the Horde, learning how to subsist off the land is just as vital as swinging an axe. Cacti growing throughout the valley yield ripe, water-rich apples that offer immediate respite from the oppressive desert sun.

Galgar, stationed inside the training grounds, has turned local foraging into an art. His famous 'Cactus Apple Surprise' is legendary among the denizens of the valley for its ability to cool a person down faster than a plunge into river water. By contracting eager recruits to harvest the prickly fruit from nearby cacti, Galgar keeps his kitchen stocked while ensuring new wanderers never set out into Durotar with an empty belly.

Galgar is an orc resident stationed within the Valley of Trials in Durotar. Rather than overseeing formal combat drills, he spends his time preparing cooling provisions and delicacies like his famous Cactus Apple Surprise to help recruits withstand the desert heat.

Foreman Thazz'ril is fed up with the Valley of Trials' workforce falling asleep on the job. Entrusted with his weighted blackjack, young recruits are tasked with roaming the valley to discipline sleeping peons and ensure vital lumber continues flowing to Durotar's settlements.

Building a new home in the arid plains of Durotar demands vast amounts of timber, stone, and sheer physical toil. Much of that burden falls squarely upon the peon caste—orcs who lack martial prowess but form the industrious backbone of the Horde. Unfortunately for Foreman Thazz'ril, the baking heat and grueling labor of the Valley of Trials make it easy for these laborers to slip off to shady trees for unauthorized naps.

Rather than allowing productivity to grind to a halt, Foreman Thazz'ril uses a rather direct management strategy: the Foreman's Blackjack. Entrusting incoming Horde recruits with this blunt disciplinary tool, he sends them across the valley floor to crack sleeping workers over the head. Startled awake, the dazed peons hastily return to chopping wood, reminded that idle hands have no place in the survival of Durotar.
Why are the peons falling asleep?
Gathering heavy lumber under Durotar's punishing sun is brutal, exhausting work. Without a supervisor breathing down their necks, peons regularly slip away beneath the shade of large trees to rest.

Peons represent the laboring class of orcish society. While physically stout, they are considered unfit for military warfare, serving instead as builders, miners, and woodcutters to fuel the Horde's war machine and settlements.

High on a southern plateau in the Valley of Trials lurks Sarkoth, an unusually vicious scorpid whose venomous sting has brought a young Darkspear hunter to death's door. Lying wounded beneath a tree, the dying troll Hana'zua pleads for a passing warrior to slay the beast and retrieve its mangled claw to salvage his honor.

The trials in the Valley are meant to temper aspiring warriors of the Horde, but the harsh desert rarely offers second chances. While stalking the valley's venomous native fauna, the young troll scout Hana'zua encountered a scorpid far larger and deadlier than the rest. Though he managed to strike a heavy blow that mangled one of its pincers, Sarkoth's tail plunged into Hana'zua's chest, leaving him bleeding out in the dry red dirt. Facing what seems to be the end of his life, his only remaining wish is that the beast does not outlive him.

Sarkoth prowls the elevated mesa overlooking the southern reaches of the Valley of Trials. Marked by the shattered claw from Hana'zua's strike, the monstrous beast dominates the high ridge, striking at anyone bold enough to climb the rocky path. Slaying the creature and returning its scarred claw to Hana'zua offers the wounded scout some bitter solace—a tangible proof that his last desperate strike softened the monster enough to be brought down.
Sarkoth prowls atop the high plateau south of where Hana'zua lies wounded. To reach him, look for a dirt ramp winding up the canyon walls, where the large scorpid wanders the ridge.

This simple rite of passage marks the moment an aspiring young champion steps forward to serve the Horde. Given by Kaltunk in the Valley of Trials, it sends untested recruits straight to Gornek to begin their basic combat training. It represents the very first step toward earning honor and survival in the harsh lands of Durotar.

In the arid canyon of the Valley of Trials, young orcs and darkspear trolls must prove their worth before they can ever set foot in the wider world. Life under Warchief Thrall demands strength, vigilance, and discipline. Kaltunk evaluates every eager recruit, temperately dampening their dreams of wrestling demons and dragons to redirect them toward realistic duties. New recruits begin their training here, learning humility before claiming glory.

Just steps away from Kaltunk sits Gornek, a gruff veteran stationed beside the camp fire. Gornek evaluates the fresh arrivals with a skeptical eye, often grumbling about the meager stock arriving at the camp. Yet, it is his responsibility to harden these fledgling fighters through rigorous trials, beginning with culling the local vermin threatening the encampment's supplies.
What is the purpose of this quest?

It serves as the introductory rite of passage for young recruits in the Valley of Trials. It officially enlists you into service under the Horde and introduces you to Gornek, who assigns your first real combat duties.
